title: The MLS Wrap: Wonderkids go international and another Messi golazo isn’t enough for Inter Miami
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Wonderkids go international and another Messi golazo isn’t enough for Inter MiamiShareAs is regularly the case, MLS fixtures continued during the international break, and some of the league’s in-form teams managed to put in strong showings despite missing several players to national team duty.
Lionel Messi leads the highlight reels once again, and two of the best teams in the division continued their good performances.
But the most notable MLS story from this round of games comes not from those league matches, but from the international window itself and the United States team that defeated Peru 4-1 on Saturday.
Mauricio Pochettino selected a squad of promising young players, including one who’s been a regular feature in this column of late, Cavan Sullivan.
The Philadelphia Union teenager, who turned 17 today, made his national team debut versus Peru and put in an impressive display, having been selected in the starting XI.
There were performances throughout the US team that showcased the homegrown talent coming through in MLS in 2026.

🇺🇸 Mauricio Pochettino gives youth a chance and the USMNT beat Peru convincingly. The starting line-up had an average age of 23. And from the bench, both Sebastian Berhalter (25) and Julian Hall (18) scored and assisted goals. pic.twitter.com/5Hl10rvsdr
The opening goal was scored by Orlando City 19-year-old attacker Justin Ellis, while the 18-year-old New England Revolution winger, Peyton Miller, started at left-back and grew into the game.
There were then numerous MLS-based international debutants off the bench, with one of them, Red Bull New York’s 18-year-old striker Julian Hall, getting the third goal in the 4-1 win.

There were also international debuts for young MLS stars Adri Mehmeti (17 years old, Red Bulls), Neil Pierre (18, Philadelphia), Brooklyn Raines (21, New England), and Frankie Westfield (20, Philadelphia).

Other foreign-based youngsters, Mathis Albert (17, Borussia Dortmund), Zavier Gozo (19, Crystal Palace), and goalkeeper Diego Kochen (20, Lyngby) also made their first senior international appearances.
But from an MLS perspective, it was encouraging that so many homegrown players have made the step up this season.

Not just to first-team football at club level, becoming regulars and in some cases key players for their teams, but also being recognised by Pochettino for international call-ups and then playing their part in a good win.
FC Dallas’ good form started to show in the overall MLS table following their 1-0 win at home to Los Angeles FC this weekend.

Both sides were missing key attackers, most notably Denis Bouanga and Son Heung-min for LAFC and Petar Musa for FC Dallas, but the team from Texas managed to keep their run going, making it four wins from their last five games.
Musa has been the outstanding player for Dallas this season. He’s ahead of Messi for goals per 90 minutes, at 0.95, and is second only to Messi for shots on target per 90.
In his absence, the FC Dallas goal came via a header from centre-back Osaze Urhoghide from a Joaquín Valiente corner.
Goalkeeper Daniel has been one of the better stoppers in MLS for several years now, and has performed well in his last two games, having joined FC Dallas from San Jose this summer.
This latest win saw them overtake St. Louis City, Houston Dynamo, New England Revolution, and Inter Miami to claim third spot in the Supporters’ Shield standings.
On the other side of the coin, this latest defeat saw LAFC make the decision to sack head coach Marc Dos Santos.
